blocks.text: Next-Gen Wiki — Living Values v1 (pared-down spec)

content.value: A wiki where canonical values live once, render live inside prose across many docs, and every doc that depends on a value shows up in an impact panel — source-of-truth-aware, impact-aware, AI-navigable. NOT pages-with-links: living documents over the graph Barkpark already has.
Amended 2026-07-01 after a 62-agent ground-truth review; 22 confirmed findings applied. Review synthesis drives the amendments.

Audience: Barkpark maintainers. Scope: the lean cut of the next-generation semantic wiki vision — reuse the existing graph, build only ONE new primitive, defer the rest. This revision folds Tasks into the same fabric under a philosophy of expectation.

One line: a wiki where canonical values live once, render live inside prose across many docs, and every doc that depends on a value shows up in an impact panel. Source-of-truth-aware, impact-aware, AI-navigable — living documents over the graph Barkpark already has, not pages with links.

blocks.text: 2. What already exists (REUSE — do not rebuild)

content.value: Every capability below already ships. The v1 job is to compose them, not re-implement them.

rows.value: content_edges table + Content.Edge + async EdgeProjector + BFS Content.Graph.traverse + backlinks reverse_referencers + /v1/graph/* + shipped blast-radius pane studio/graph_view.ex; kind is free-string so a new relation type needs ZERO migration
reverse_referencers + traverse + dangling/orphans, already shipped and consumed
revisions table snapshots the whole doc on every mutation; draft/published lifecycle
Canonical value rendered from a resolver (block-level)
field-reference + codelist already resolve a value from another doc at render via an injected resolver (render.ex:130-168, fields.go:108-131)
acceptance_criteria (the expectation primitive — already present, inert)
already [{criterion, met, evidence}] on every task (tasks/schema.ex:224) — declared, stored, shape-validated
100% ADVISORY: nothing reads met/evidence; a task closes with all criteria unmet (close.ex never references it; validation.ex:126 only shape-checks). THE expectation primitive exists as inert data.
auto-projects a content_edges edge of kind 'design_doc' via the generic reference-field extractor (content/edges.ex:221)

The paper<->task graph link EXISTS; nobody has pointed impact traversal inward yet. Projects only when the task doc is PUBLISHED — which the bp task lifecycle never does (tasks stay status: draft by design). Any demo of this edge must publish the task docs first via the generic publish API.

task_edges = CLOSED allowlist {blocks, discovered-from}, task<->task only, drives ready-gating + cascading unblock (close.ex:152) + fencing-epoch close. content_edges = OPEN kinds; tasks + their design_doc/parent_id/attachments references participate
Reuse both, separately — expectations/values ride content_edges; the gating DAG stays in task_edges.

WriteScope.fire_after (write_scope.ex:338-361) enqueues reprojection on generic Content.Writer saves and publish/unpublish/delete — but NOT on the paper block-op writers (upsert_paper / apply_paper_block_op / apply_paper_block_ops, block_ops.ex:197-202, 334, 444), which do raw Repo writes. Those are exactly the paths the Studio canvas and Bulldocs ingest use. Wiring reprojection into those three writers is net-new (wire §7).
The event seam for 'reflag on edit' EXISTS; the reaction does not.
tasks do NOT have PortableDoc block bodies today — description/design are plain-text fields (schema.ex:184,193); papers DO have PortableDoc bodies
Gap — blocks tasks-in-tasks; deliver tasks-in-papers first.

blocks.text: 3. Track A — Values — the ONE loop (v1 scope)

items.value: Canonical value = a document / typed field (EXISTS).

Inline live-reference = ONE new inline node type that renders the CURRENT value in running prose, reusing the existing field-reference/codelist resolver seam. A live-rendered value can't go stale on surfaces that resolve at request time; the public reader's write-time body_html cache and pre-rendered delta frames stay stale until the referencing paper is re-edited (see wire §Freshness).
Used-by / impact = reverse_referencers + traverse (read side SHIPPED; the edges themselves require the net-new body-walk extractor — wire §7).

Stale detection = ONE comparison (fallback literal vs resolved value) computed inside the render-time pre-resolve pass. The plugin checkers seam (Barkpark.Validation.Checker) is a pure value-validation behaviour with no Repo access and structurally cannot resolve target.field on another document — no standalone checker.
Who fills it = AI proposes marks/values as DRAFTS; human/authorized agent approves via the existing draft→publish gate (that IS 'Review' — no new state machine).
Provenance = every AI assertion carries a source edge; NEVER overwrite prose.

content.value: Blocks have stable ids + id-addressed patch ops and survive edits; character offsets drift the instant prose is edited and would silently rot every claim built on them. Sub-block character ranges are deferred until a real use case proves block-grain too coarse. This is recorded as decided, not open.

items.value: Range is research-grade (collaborative-anchoring / drift). Block-anchoring sidesteps it for v1.
Who writes observations is the graveyard of semantic wikis; the AI-suggestion-with-provenance loop + human gate is the answer, not a schema.
Contradiction is only 'structural' if both sides are pre-structured; comparing free prose to a value is NLP-hard, not a graph query. The marking is the cost.

FOUR surfaces must land in lockstep: Elixir api/lib/barkpark/portable_doc/render/inline.ex (raises), Go internal/pdrender/inline.go (blanks childless unknowns), React web/components/portable-doc.tsx (vanishes), AND the Studio paper editor's TipTap converter api/assets/paper-editor/src/convert.js (drops childless unknown inline nodes on load and rewrites the block's whole content on save — one keystroke in a paragraph containing the node deletes it permanently, in both the per-block editor and the prod-enabled canvas). The TS kernel cited at render.ex:4-5 does not exist in this repo — record it as retired or locate it before counting surfaces. Repo-side owner for this contract: docs/contracts/portable-doc-inline.md.

Today's edges come from schema reference FIELDS, not marked prose. 'Marked text → edge' is a new extraction path; blockref (block-id anchor) is the existing sub-doc link and the hint to anchor at block grain.
Character-offset ranges + overlapping marks
Observation table with confidence floats
Review state machine
Concept & Context node kinds
Declaring 13 node kinds / 10 edge verbs up front (let kind accrete)
All heatmaps / visualization
Tasks get PortableDoc block bodies (prerequisite for tasks-in-tasks) — deferred
Reflag-on-paper-edit reactor — deferred until surfacing proves demand
Hard close-enforcement of acceptance_criteria — deferred (surface first, enforce later)
PERMANENTLY deferred: merging the two edge tables (task_edges stays separate from content_edges — never merge)
Marked text → semantic truth
Source-of-truth-aware
Never silently overwrite prose
AI suggestions are marked as suggestions
Provenance on every machine assertion
Edit a canonical value in ONE place.
Every doc that inline-references it renders the new value.
The impact/used-by panel lists the N docs that depend on it.
A pinned literal that drifted from canonical is flagged by the checker.
Expectation demo: a paper claim marked as an expectation drives a task.

Expectation demo: closing that task with evidence flips the claim to 'satisfied' in the paper's reverse view. Mechanism: close/3 writes only lifecycle_status/claim/close_reason (close.ex:103-146); setting met/evidence is a separate content mutation racing the close's rev CAS — scoped into lvw-t9 (agent/CLI mutates criteria at close time; the 'satisfied' flip is the t8 reverse view re-reading).
(post-v1 — deferred: demos the reflag reactor §6 defers, and §2's seam claim does not hold for paper edits per amendment 2) Expectation demo: editing the paper claim re-flags the dependent task.
Precondition: task-side graph demo steps require the demo task docs to be PUBLISHED (projection is published-perspective only; all lvw docs are drafts; the live graph has 0 edges today).

content.value: All on top of existing graph/backlinks/lifecycle; only ONE new inline NODE TYPE + ONE drift comparison are net-new node/check primitives for Track A — plus the resolver extensions on each surface, the body-walk edge extractor with its reprojection wiring and backfill, the paper-editor converter mapping, and the server-pre-resolve plumbing (wire §5/§7). The expectation track adds no new store — it reads the acceptance_criteria and design_doc primitives that already ship.

blocks.text: 9. Papers<->Tasks unification — the philosophy of expectation

content.value: acceptance_criteria = expectation: criterion = the claim that must become true, met = the observation, evidence = the provenance. It is already the shape; it is just inert.
Values and Expectations are the SAME pattern at two grains: a canonical thing + an inline live reference + an impact graph + provenance + review-on-change.

items.value: Paper drives Task: an unmet expectation IS the reason a task is open.
Task proves Paper: closing the task sets met=true + evidence = the observation.
Misalignment: paper edited → expectation unsatisfied → reflag the dependent tasks.

content.value: Net effect: Papers and Tasks are ONE PortableDoc fabric over ONE truth graph, not two systems.

items.value: wikilink (whole doc) + blockref (block-id anchor = block-grain range) already cross types; the resolver is type-agnostic. This is the reuse.

Inline task-reference CHIP: a type-aware resolver renders live task state (status / priority / criteria-progress) instead of a title, for a wikilink/blockref whose target is a task. This delivers 'reference tasks inside papers.' Three renderers in lockstep: Elixir inline.ex, Go inline.go, React portable-doc.tsx.

'Tasks inside tasks' needs tasks to GAIN a PortableDoc body (today they have plain-text description/design) → schema + Studio editor change → DEFERRED. Deliver tasks-in-papers first (paper bodies already exist).

Rich chip state (status/priority/criteria) resolves for anonymous readers only when the target task doc is PUBLISHED; otherwise the chip degrades to title/alias — matching the published-perspective pin for anonymous callers (query_controller.ex:288).
Read-side live-render can't drift and is safe (v1). Write-through (edit a ref → mutate the canonical → propagate to every mention) is powerful and dangerous.
It is this spec's own 'never silently overwrite prose' rule INVERTED: a prose edit silently rewriting shared truth that gates OTHER docs' tasks.
Don't skip it; GATE it: an explicit edit-through affordance (you KNOW you're editing the shared value) + an impact preview ('changes N docs') + provenance + review on high-impact change.
(1) Edit-through authorization is evaluated against the TARGET canonical doc's write scope — write access to the hosting paper grants nothing; unauthorized/cross-scope target disables the affordance.

(2) The 'changes N docs' impact preview MUST be produced by Content.Graph.reverse_referencers/2 called with the caller's scope opts, inheriting its existing MEDIUM-5 fail-closed posture: out-of-scope referencers are dropped entirely — no titles, no stub, and NO aggregate 'K you cannot see' count.

content.value: Do NOT merge the two edge tables. blocks-gating is correctness-critical (ready queue, cascading unblock, fencing). Expectations/values ride content_edges; the DAG stays in task_edges.
Graduated enforcement, not a hard gate. Tasks close freely today; read & SURFACE unmet criteria (a warning, like the existing soft cross_validations schema.ex:106) before ever enforcing on close.
Bound the reflag reactor. Reuse the graph engine's existing depth-clamp / node-budget; no unbounded cascade.

Writeback must be gated: explicit edit-through affordance + impact preview ('changes N docs') + provenance + review on high-impact change. Edit-through authorization is evaluated against the TARGET canonical doc's write scope; the 'changes N docs' impact preview is produced by reverse_referencers with the caller's scope opts, fail-closed, with no aggregate 'you cannot see' count.
Tasks lack bodies → deliver tasks-in-papers first, tasks-in-tasks later.

items.value: D1 — Body-walk edges are publish-gated in v1: the plugin-seam extractor feeds only the published materialised graph; a follow-up task (lvw-t12) folds Registry.collect_edge_extractors into build_drafts_indexes for the drafts graph. Rationale: keeps v1 off the drafts-fold complexity and the demo's critical path.

D2 — Public-reader freshness: inject the value/task resolvers into BulldocsLive's mount/refetch render, resolved as the anonymous principal — per-page-load freshness, no live push. Rationale: fresh without building a dependent-refresh reactor.

D3 — valueref target = doc_id slug, resolved via resolve_doc_pk with published-row preference (DraftId.published_id normalization). Rationale: matches every other body reference, survives export/import, and coalesces draft/published.

D4 — Drift-accept: a Studio 'accept new baseline' affordance issuing an ifRev-guarded fallback-only patch with provenance. Rationale: the CAS already ships (412 on rev mismatch); no parallel ack store.
D5 — Rich task-chip state resolves anonymously only for PUBLISHED task docs; otherwise degrade to title/alias. Rationale: matches the published-perspective pin and closes a token-gate bypass.

D6 — Authoring dual-writes the fallback as a {type:"text", value:<fallback>} child so old bp binaries degrade to visible text; new renderers ignore valueref children. Rationale: preserves the never-blank invariant retroactively at one dual-write cost.
